newsitem.title: UK: UK utility Eurobond spreads steady on Labour win.
newsitem.headline: UK utility Eurobond spreads steady on Labour win.

text.p: Spreads on sterling Eurobonds issued by British utilities were steady on Friday, although their share prices fell on windfall tax fears after Labour's landslide election victory.

Dealers said a windfall tax of up to five billion stg on water and electricity companies had already been factored into bond spreads, and they were unlikely to move unless Labour decided to tax more heavily.
"Utility spreads have not moved -- the windfall tax has been well-flagged and was already priced in last year," a Eurosterling trader said. "We are not seeing any sizeable flows at all."
British water and electricity companies are active borrowers in the sterling Eurobond market.
A benchmark for the shorter maturity issues is an Eastern Electricity, a unit of Energy Group, 8.375 percent 2004 bond which was trading at 62 basis points over gilts at 0930 GMT.
An Eastern Electricity 8.75 percent 2012, a benchmark for the longer end, was trading at 81 b.p. over gilts.

Other utilities with sterling bonds outstanding include Anglian Water Plc, East Midlands Electricity Plc, London Electricity Plc, National Grid Group Plc, National Power Plc, Northern Electric Plc, PowerGen Plc, and South Wales Electricity Plc.
Their shares were down slightly, although equity analysts said there was no real selling pressure and prices could come back quickly.
They said utilities would face a few months of uncertainty while the market waits for exactly how Labour decides to levy the tax.

The sterling Eurobond sector was generally subdued, with spreads steady across the board. Traders said turnover volumes were low, and were unlikely to pick up until next week when British investors return from Monday's public holiday.
The Labour party came to power on Friday in a landslide election victory which toppled the Conservative party after 18 years of rule.
